<context>
You are an expert at solving ARC-AGI (Abstraction and Reasoning Corpus) puzzles using Answer Set Programming (ASP).

ARC-AGI puzzles show input-output grid transformations. Each cell contains a color value (integer 0–9). The goal is to discover the hidden transformation rule from training examples and encode it as an ASP program.
</context>

<rules>
- `input(row, col, color)` facts are injected automatically — do not define them.
- `color(0..9)` facts are injected automatically — do not define them.
- the output predicate is always `output(row, col, color)` — do not redefine it.
- the final program must produce exactly one answer set, in which `output(row, col, color)` match the expected output exactly.
- end your program with `#show output/3.`
</rules>

<example_1>
This puzzle copies the input to the output unchanged.

<grid_1>
Input:
<diagram>
0 1 0
2 0 3
0 4 0
</diagram>

Output:
<diagram>
0 1 0
2 0 3
0 4 0
</diagram>
</grid_1>

<asp>
% Grid dimensions
n_rows(N) :- N = #count{ R : input(R, _, _) }.
n_cols(N) :- N = #count{ C : input(_, C, _) }.
row(0..N-1) :- n_rows(N).
col(0..M-1) :- n_cols(M).

% Output has the same dimensions as the input
output_cell(R, C) :- row(R), col(C).

% Each output cell gets exactly one color
1 { output(R, C, Color) : color(Color) } 1 :- output_cell(R, C).

% Copy each input cell to the output unchanged
output(R, C, Color) :- input(R, C, Color).

#show output/3.
</asp>
</example_1>

<example_2>
This puzzle replaces every non-zero cell with color 5; zero cells stay 0.

<grid_1>
Input:
<diagram>
0 1 0
2 0 3
0 4 0
</diagram>

Output:
<diagram>
0 5 0
5 0 5
0 5 0
</diagram>
</grid_1>

<asp>
% Grid dimensions
n_rows(N) :- N = #count{ R : input(R, _, _) }.
n_cols(N) :- N = #count{ C : input(_, C, _) }.
row(0..N-1) :- n_rows(N).
col(0..M-1) :- n_cols(M).

% Output has the same dimensions as the input
output_cell(R, C) :- row(R), col(C).

% Each output cell gets exactly one color
1 { output(R, C, Color) : color(Color) } 1 :- output_cell(R, C).

% Recolor every non-zero cell to 5; zeros stay 0.
output(R, C, 5) :- input(R, C, V), V != 0.
output(R, C, 0) :- input(R, C, 0).

#show output/3.
</asp>
</example_2>

<asp>
% Grid dimensions
n_rows(N) :- N = #count{ R : input(R, _, _) }.
n_cols(N) :- N = #count{ C : input(_, C, _) }.
row(0..N-1) :- n_rows(N).
col(0..M-1) :- n_cols(M).

% Output has the same dimensions as the input
output_cell(R, C) :- row(R), col(C).

% Each output cell gets exactly one color
1 { output(R, C, Color) : color(Color) } 1 :- output_cell(R, C).

% Mirror: column C of the output is column (M-1-C) of the input.
output(R, C, Color) :- input(R, Cin, Color), n_cols(M), C = M - 1 - Cin.

#show output/3.
</asp>
</example_3>

% ---------- Grid dimensions ----------
n_rows(N) :- N = #count{ R : input(R, _, _) }.
n_cols(M) :- M = #count{ C : input(_, C, _) }.
row(R)    :- n_rows(N), R = 0..N-1.
col(C)    :- n_cols(M), C = 0..M-1.

output_cell(R,C) :- row(R), col(C).

% ---------- Reachability for colour 2 ----------
% vertical (down) from any 2
reachable2_vert(R,C) :- input(R,C,2).
reachable2_vert(R,C) :- reachable2_vert(R1,C), R1 = R - 1, input(R,C,0).

% horizontal (right) from any 2
reachable2_horiz(R,C) :- input(R,C,2).
reachable2_horiz(R,C) :- reachable2_horiz(R,C1), C1 = C - 1, input(R,C,0).

% horizontal (left) from any 2
reachable2_left(R,C) :- input(R,C,2).
reachable2_left(R,C) :- reachable2_left(R,C1), C1 = C + 1, input(R,C,0).

% ---------- Reachability for colour 8 ----------
% vertical (down) from any 8
reachable8_vert(R,C) :- input(R,C,8).
reachable8_vert(R,C) :- reachable8_vert(R1,C), R1 = R - 1, input(R,C,0).

% horizontal (right) from any 8
reachable8_horiz(R,C) :- input(R,C,8).
reachable8_horiz(R,C) :- reachable8_horiz(R,C1), C1 = C - 1, input(R,C,0).

% horizontal (left) from any 8
reachable8_left(R,C) :- input(R,C,8).
reachable8_left(R,C) :- reachable8_left(R,C1), C1 = C + 1, input(R,C,0).

% ---------- Both‑reachable combinations ----------
both_reachable(R,C) :- reachable2_vert(R,C), reachable8_horiz(R,C).
both_reachable(R,C) :- reachable2_horiz(R,C), reachable8_vert(R,C).
both_reachable(R,C) :- reachable2_left(R,C), reachable8_horiz(R,C).
both_reachable(R,C) :- reachable2_horiz(R,C), reachable8_left(R,C).

% ---------- Output definition ----------
% Copy the original colour for every non‑zero cell
output(R,C,Color) :- input(R,C,Color), Color != 0.

% Zero cells become 3 if a 2‑source and an 8‑source can reach the cell
output(R,C,3) :- input(R,C,0), both_reachable(R,C).

% Otherwise the cell stays 0
output(R,C,0) :- input(R,C,0), not both_reachable(R,C).

% Exactly one colour per cell
1 { output(R,C,Color) : color(Color) } 1 :- output_cell(R,C).

#show output/3.

n_rows(N) :- N = #count{ R : input(R, _, _) }.
n_cols(M) :- M = #count{ C : input(_, C, _) }.
row(R) :- n_rows(N), R = 0..N-1.
col(C) :- n_cols(M), C = 0..M-1.

output(R,C,0) :- input(R,C,0), not both_reachable(R,C).
output(R,C,Color) :- input(R,C,Color), Color != 0.

% exactly one output per cell
1 { output(R,C,Color) : color(Color) } 1 :- output_cell(R,C).
